infection of MRSA. The number of patients infected with MRSA has increased in
some hospitals. Suggest two ways to reduce the transmission of MRSA in hospitals.

questions.answerText:
(a) The bacterial cell walls become fragile due to the lack of peptidoglycan. (1)
The bacterial cell walls are not tough enough to limit the influx of water by
osmosis into the bacterial cells. (1)
The bacterial cells eventually burst due to the excessive influx of water. (1)
(b) Within a population of Staphylococcus aureus, some bacteria have antibiotic
resistance while others do not. (1)
The antibiotic resistant bacteria produce the enzyme beta-lactamase which breaks
the structure of antibiotics and thus these bacteria are not killed, while the non-
resistant bacteria are killed by the antibiotics. (1)
Facing less competition for resources, the antibiotic-resistant bacteria reproduce
rapidly and their number increases. (1)
Finally, the whole population of bacteria becomes resistant to the antibiotic. (1)
(c) Prescribe antibiotics together with a drug that inhibits the action of the enzyme
beta-lactamase. (1)
The activity of beta-lactamase would be greatly reduced, thus the antibiotics would
remain intact to exert bactericidal effect. (1)
(d) Any two of the following: (2)
 Manage wounds properly by keeping wounds sterilized and covering them
with waterproof adhesive dressings.
 Wash hands with liquid soap and water before and after touching wounds.
 Perform hand hygiene frequently, especially after touching public installations
such as handrails or door knobs.
(Or other reasonable answers)

questions.text:
The occurrence of mutations is random and mutations can be beneficial, harmful or
neutral to organisms. Under the action of natural selection, characteristics favourable for
survival in the environment are selected.
(a) Explain what is meant by a mutation. (1 mark)
(b) Mutations can be classified as spontaneous and induced mutations. State one cause
for each type of mutations. (2 marks)
(c) Explain how mutation could be beneficial to organisms. (3 marks)
(d) Explain how harmful mutations may weaken or kill an organism by affecting its
metabolic activities. (3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a) A mutation is a sudden and permanent change in the DNA of an organism. (1)
(b) Spontaneous mutation arises from errors in DNA replication. (1)
Induced mutation is caused by exposure to mutagens (e.g. X-rays / gamma rays /
ultra-violet radiation, etc.). (1)
(c) Mutations can give genetic variations in organisms. (1)
Some genetic variations are favourable for the survival of organisms in their
environment. (1)
The individuals with the mutant genes for favourable characters have a greater
chance to survive and reproduce. (1)
(d) Mutations may result in the production of abnormal proteins which are not
functional. (1)
Hence, mutations may affect enzymes or other proteins that are essential for
metabolism. (1)
Metabolic activities are controlled by enzymes or other essential proteins. The lack
of these proteins would inhibit metabolic activities. (1)
________
(9 marks)

IA and IB are co-dominant while allele i is recessive to both.

(a) What is the blood group genotype of the father? Explain your answer. (4 marks)
(b) State all the possible blood group(s) of the mother. (1 mark)
Red-green colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait in humans. In the family, the
father is red-green colour-blind while the mother is a carrier of the allele for red-green
colour blindness.
(c) This couple has recently given birth to a daughter. What is the chance of their
daughter being red-green colour-blind? Explain your answer. (3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a) Since the father is of blood group A, he must have at least one allele IA. (1)
The son is of blood group B. It is not possible for him to have an allele IA, and the
father must have passed an allele i to the son. (1)
Thus, the genotype of the father is IA i. (1)
(b) Blood groups B and AB (1)
(c) The father is red-green colour-blind. He must have an X chromosome bearing the
allele for red-green colour blindness and must pass this X chromosome to his
daughter. (1)
The mother is a carrier. She must have an allele for red-green colour blindness on
one of her X chromosomes, and a normal allele on the other. (1)
The daughter will be red-green colour-blind if she receives the X chromosome
bearing the allele for red-green colour blindness from her mother. Hence there is a
1/ (or 50%) chance for her to be red-green colour-blind. (1)

A person likes his plants and pet dog very much, and is thinking about cloning them. He
is discussing his idea with a scientist.

biotechnology. (1 mark)
(ii) Describe a suitable cloning method if the person would like to make cloned
plants free of pathogens. (4 marks)
(b) Concerning the process of animal cloning using nuclear transfer, explain why
cloning the person’s pet dog is ethically more controversial than cloning plants.
(2 marks)
© 2024 Aristo Educational Press Ltd. - 9 -
(c) The scientist suggests another method. In this method, the person’s pet dog breeds
with another dog with similar desirable traits that the person likes.
(i) In terms of the means by which new lives are formed, explain why this
method is less controversial than animal cloning. (2 marks)
(ii) Widespread practice of the method of breeding animals with similar traits
may give rise to inbreeding. State how inbreeding and animal cloning can
lead to health problems in the animals reproduced respectively. (2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a) (i) Artificial propagation (1)
(ii) Obtain sterilized explants from the parent plant. (1)
Culture the explant in a sterile culture medium with plant hormones and
essential nutrients, forming a callus. (1)
Culture pieces of callus in another sterile culture medium containing plant
hormones, forming plantlets. (1)
Plant the plantlets formed in the soil. (1)
(b) Cloning animals often involves the destruction of unsuccessfully cloned embryos,
while cloning plants do not involve the formation of embryos. (1)
Cloning animals raises the ethical problem of sacrificing embryos for only a small

However, animal cloning artificially gives rise to new lives, instead of using
natural biological mechanisms of reproduction. (1)

Inbreeding easily gives rise to offspring with health defects related to
